adds.title: Movement Advancement Project - Wisconsin's Equality Profile
adds.summary: As of 2025-05-29 Wisconsin had no statewide public-accommodations nondiscrimination protection based on gender identity with only 21% of the population covered by full local employment-housing-public-accommodations ordinances in 10 cities and 12% by partial ordinances, had no law banning transgender people from using government-building bathrooms or facilities consistent with gender identity, no law defining sex to exclude transgender people, no drag-performance restriction, no ban on best-practice medical care for transgender youth and no shield law while private insurance and Medicaid were barred from excluding transgender-specific care, had a hate-crime law covering sexual orientation but not gender identity, and permitted limited gender-marker change on driver's licenses while restricting change on birth certificates with no X gender-neutral option on either and a restrictive name-change process.

adds.title: Wyoming House Bill 72 - public restroom biological sex segregation (2025)
adds.summary: Wyoming enacted House Bill 72 signed by Governor Mark Gordon on March 3, 2025 after 52-8 House passage on February 7, 2025 and 25-6 Senate passage, effective July 1, 2025, defining male and female by biological sex and requiring public facilities to reserve multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters exclusively for males or exclusively for females and prohibiting entry into facilities not matching biological sex, allowing only reasonable accommodations that do not include opposite-sex multi-occupancy access, and creating a cause of action for a person encountering an opposite-sex person in a sex-designated restroom or changing area where the facility permitted it or failed to prohibit it and for a person required by a correctional or educational facility to share sleeping quarters with the opposite sex.

adds.title: Wyoming transgender athlete ban (2023 Legislature)
adds.summary: On March 1, 2023, the Wyoming Legislature approved SF133 banning transgender students from playing sports consistent with their gender identity and advanced the bill to Governor Mark Gordon's desk.
